title: Hazel and the Landfall
premise: Bush pilot Sebastian Yarrow crashes on a drowned coastline where the receding tide has exposed a sea cave tied to a vanished mining dynasty — and to the inheritance of the stranger who pulls him from the surf, a woman named Hazel whose family legend says the cave holds proof her grandfather's fortune was stolen. Trapped by the monsoon with a leaking boat and rival claimants closing in, Sebastian and Hazel must decide whether loyalty to the people who raised them matters more than the truth rotting inside the rock. The corrupt heir who engineered their stranding follows them into the cave for a final confrontation as the tide returns; he is lost to the water, and Hazel chooses to publish the truth rather than claim the fortune, flying out with Sebastian as equals.
about_author: Hazel Pemberton spent a decade ferrying supplies across coastal Alaska before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the salt-bleached cadence of someone who has trusted weather more than people. She writes from a floating cabin she refuses to give directions to.

chapters.title: Freight and Rumors
chapters.summary: Sebastian Yarrow's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior introduces his world: unreliable clients, a debt-ridden airfield, and rumors of a mining family's lost fortune that everyone repeats but no one believes. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness; he takes one last charter he shouldn't.

chapters.title: The Tide Takes Something Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flying the charter along a storm-bruised coast, he spots an impossible opening in the cliffs — a cave exposed by an anomalous low tide — before engine trouble forces him down in the shallows. He survives the crash but loses the plane. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the wilderness shows him something it meant to keep hidden.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Pulled Him Out
chapters.summary: Hazel Vane's POV. Hazel drags a half-drowned pilot from the surf to her decaying family boathouse, recognizing the cave he describes as the one from her grandfather's forbidden stories. She hides him from passing boats. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual need; she decides the stranger is her way back into the cave.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Hazel reveals the legend: her grandfather's partner stole the mine's profits, and proof lies sealed in the cave. Sebastian recognizes the name of the current claimant — Aldous Crane, the man who chartered his flight. Emotional beat: the slow realization that neither of them found this place by accident.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They set out by boat ahead of the monsoon; sabotage discovered mid-channel — a plug pulled, radio dead — strands them on a shingle beach as the storm hits. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Sebastian realizes someone wanted them marooned, not dead. Yet.

chapters.title: Crane
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Aldous Crane arrives at the beach under the flag of rescue, all charm and offers: sign away any claim, and he'll fly them out. Hazel plays along while Sebastian finds evidence Crane sabotaged the boat. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety versus the cost of complicity; loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Into the Rock
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Under cover of the storm's worst night, they slip past Crane's men and enter the cave at low tide, navigating flooded galleries to a sealed chamber holding ledgers, letters, and a confession proving the theft — and naming Hazel's grandmother as a co-conspirator. Emotional beat: truth arriving uglier than hoped; inheritance revealed as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The tide turns early and traps them inside as Crane, tipped off by a traitor among Hazel's few allies, enters behind them. Cornered in the dark with rising water, they bargain, then fight. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror; every secret between Sebastian and Hazel surfaces with the water.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax. In the flooding outer gallery, Crane tries to seize the ledgers and is swept out with the surge when he refuses Sebastian's offered hand — the wilderness forgiving nothing. Sebastian and Hazel escape through a blowhole passage as the cave seals itself forever. Emotional beat: grief without regret; the price of greed paid in full.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Resolution. With the storm broken, they salvage the boat and reach the mainland, where Hazel publishes the confession instead of pressing a claim to the fortune, freeing herself from the inheritance entirely. Sebastian rebuilds his airfield with her as partner. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — loyalty kept by choosing truth over what it could have bought.
